dedupe_keys.name: a comprehensive dataset for australian mine production 1799 to 2021 mudd

description: This dataset compiles Australian mine production from 1799 to 2021 at mine level, including ore processed, grades, extracted products such as metals, concentrates and saleable ore, and waste rock. The DataCite record says national statistics usually cover only single commodities, and that this is a first national compilation of basic mining data, meant for assessing mineable resources, environmental impacts, material flows and critical mineral potential, including recovery from tailings and waste rock. Version 2 was published on 30 May 2023 by Gavin Mudd of RMIT University as a master Excel workbook of about 0.9 MB and CSV tables of notes, a summary, mine-by-mine data, annual data and tin fields, with graphs for gold, copper, silver, lead, zinc and nickel, all downloadable and free under CC BY 4.0. Coverage is national for Australia. Caveats: data are compiled from many historical sources of varying quality, and the exact list of commodities and the update plan are not stated on the page read. For simulation it gives long production histories per mine to build mining supply scenarios, to estimate tailings and waste rock stocks that feed hazard and reprocessing studies, and to calibrate material flow models of metals. Related catalogue records include the Australian Mine Waste Database, the Geoscience Australia OZMIN mineral deposits database and the BGS World Mineral Statistics.
